models.name: Muse Glimmer 30B (CoreAI)
models.summary: Meta's 30B-parameter on-device agentic language model optimized for Apple Silicon via Apple's CoreAI runtime with DFlash speculative decoding (K=4 drafter), ANE/GPU heterogeneous dispatch, and Meta ATEM XML tool calling / reasoning streaming.

variants.name: Muse Glimmer 30B (4-bit, DFlash K=4 Drafter)

download.note: 55.49 GiB (59,581,829,216 bytes) upstream checkpoint download from Hugging Face meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B at pinned commit SHA a4e59da52a7b before local 4-bit quantization (~15.2 GB) and pairing with 5-layer DFlash speculative drafter from meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-assistant.

working_set.note: 18.5 GiB estimated peak unified memory working set on Apple Silicon: ~15.0 GiB fused 4-bit weights, ring KV cache, 5-layer DFlash drafter hidden state buffers across target layers [1, 13, 25, 37, 49], and short-context agent scratchpad.

variants.notes:
DFlash speculative decoding drafter with two-phase inference: 1. inject_kv writes target encoder features into the ring KV cache via per-layer
   Wk/Wv projections.
2. draft executes bidirectional attention over injected context and mask tokens,
   producing K=4 token predictions in a single forward pass.
Performance: Acceptance rate at K=4 is 64% (~1.85x generation speedup), verified against HF MuseGlimmerAssistantModel at all 24 sub-layer checkpoints. Heterogeneous Dispatch: Partitions the 5-layer sliding-window drafter to Apple Neural Engine (ANE, 2-5W low power) and target causal transformer layers to Metal GPU without memory copying over unified memory. Agentic Tool Calling: Supports Meta ATEM XML protocol (to=self for reasoning_content, to=<tool> with <atem:function_calls> for function invocation, to=user for visible content) exposed over llm-server OpenAI-compatible SSE streaming endpoint. Memory Fit: Fits comfortably on Apple Silicon unified memory configurations >= 24GB (runs_well on 36GB / 48GB / 64GB+ unified memory).

download.note: RRDBNet x4plus generator weights

working_set.note: Model weights resident with full-resolution patch tiled inference buffer

models.name: Sana
models.summary: Deep-compression linear diffusion transformer capable of generating 4K resolution images with low latency.

download.note: Linear DiT weights and 32x autoencoder checkpoints

working_set.note: Deep compression linear DiT working set during 1024px generation (~5.5 GB VRAM)

models.name: SeedVR2
models.summary: ByteDance Seed's diffusion-based video and image upscaler/restorer, not a text-to-image model — mflux runs it as a restoration pass rather than a generator. Packaged for ComfyUI by numz; both the wrapper and the upstream ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR project are Apache 2.0.

variants.name: SeedVR2 3B

working_set.note: download size (fp16 + fp8 checkpoints plus the shared VAE) plus a 20% margin; no measured run on any machine. A single precision loaded at once would use roughly half this.

variants.notes: Faster, lower-VRAM variant. mflux aliases "seedvr2-3b", "seedvr2" (the bare alias defaults to 3B).

variants.name: SeedVR2 7B

working_set.note: download size (fp16, fp8, and "sharp" fp16/fp8 checkpoints plus the shared VAE) plus a 20% margin; no measured run on any machine. A single precision loaded at once would use a fraction of this — the repo carries every variant, this figure does not.

variants.notes: Higher-quality, higher-VRAM variant, plus a "sharp" checkpoint. mflux alias "seedvr2-7b" (and "seedvr2-7B").

models.name: SenseVoice
models.summary: Non-autoregressive streaming foundation speech understanding model from Alibaba Tongyi Lab. 15x faster than Whisper with multi-task audio event detection, rich emotion tagging, and multilingual transcription.

working_set.note: ~600 MiB working set on Apple Silicon Metal

models.name: Wan 2.1
models.summary: Alibaba's text-to-video family. The 1.3B is the smallest genuinely open video model that is worth running.

working_set.note: 8.19 GB peak GPU memory, stated on the official model card at https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B for a 5-second 480p generation. Replaces our earlier 11 GB estimate; the card is describing the same bf16 weights this variant downloads.

speed.note: About 4 minutes for a 5-second 480p clip, stated on the official model card at https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B without quantisation or other optimisation. Not measured by us.

variants.name: Wan 2.1 T2V 14B

working_set.note: transformer weights plus text encoder and VAE held resident, no measured run on any machine yet

variants.notes: Beyond any single consumer card and beyond every Apple Silicon configuration currently sold.

models.name: Wan 2.2
models.summary: The only video model here under a licence with no revenue cap and no territory exclusion. That makes it the safe default even where it is not the fastest.

working_set.note: transformer weights plus text encoder and VAE held resident, no measured run on any machine yet

speed.note: 82 minutes for a 2-second clip in GGUF, reported at https://lilting.ch/en/articles/ltx2-wan22-mac-local-video-gen — third-party, on twice the memory of a 32 GB machine. Not measured by us. Treat as the order of magnitude, not the number.

models.name: Z-Image

variants.notes: mflux aliases "z-image", "zimage".

working_set.note: download size plus a 20% margin for the text encoder and VAE held resident during generation; no measured run on any machine.

variants.name: Z-Image Turbo ControlNet Union 2.1

working_set.note: base Z-Image-Turbo repo (32899667397 bytes) plus this ControlNet repo (53146322472 bytes), plus a 20% margin for encoders held resident; no measured run on any machine.
